source_span: You potentially have a supply shock hurting growth at the same time as the Fed is pushed toward tightening. Not a great backdrop for multiples.
source_chain: Crude/gas/product prices break out on Hormuz escalation, therefore front-end yields (not just the long end/term premium) get pulled up as the market prices a real Fed response, therefore a supply shock is hurting growth at the same moment it pushes the Fed toward tightening, therefore that is a poor backdrop for equity multiples. Invalidation: if the administration gets crude/gas/product prices lower (per GS's own de-escalation-history precedent and possibly-normalizing shipping flows), yields stabilize and risk can recover, provided NFP/CPI cooperate; if energy keeps rising, the Fed gets dragged along and sustained upside gets much harder.
pulse_chain: Brent/gas/diesel break out, therefore government bond yields hit multi-year highs across the curve including the 2-year as traders price a real chance of a September Fed hike, therefore Goldman frames this as the bad version of an energy move: a supply shock hurting growth at the same moment it pushes the Fed toward tightening, therefore that's a poor setting for equity multiples (JPM disputes the read, arguing yields reflect activity not de-anchoring inflation expectations, given soft wage growth, and expects less tightening than priced). Invalidation: Goldman's own test — if crude/gas/product prices come down, yields stabilize and risk assets recover provided Friday's payrolls and Sept 11 CPI cooperate, consistent with GS's escalation-history pattern and possibly-normalizing shipping flows; if energy keeps climbing, sustained equity upside gets much harder.
why: The pulse reproduces GS's supply-shock-meets-Fed-tightening chain and its own de-escalation/payrolls-CPI invalidation with correct attribution, and layers in JPM's opposing read as a counterpoint without altering GS's argued steps or direction.
